relevance_note: Single case report of an ALDH5A1 compound heterozygote with SSADH deficiency: "We report a patient with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory, every value from my reading, every span checked verbatim by script. In-scope people: the proband (label 'patient', single unnamed case-report patient), her brother (carrier, isolated speech delay) and both parents (each carries one of the mutations; sexes of the two parent rows are not assignable to a specific mutation, so labelled 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2' with sex not reported, per the label rule for unsexed 'parents'). The Markdown renders '>' as '>'; spans keep '>' as in the file, values use '>' as printed in the article (c.278 G>T, c.1557 T>G). Protein descriptions appear twice: 'p.Cys93>Phe' and 'p. Tyr519X' in the Case Report, 'p.Cys93Phe' and 'p.Tyr519X' in the Discussion; values use the Discussion forms, both spans given. Patient inheritance recorded as 'inherited unspecified parent' for both variants: the paper says each parent carries one mutation but not which parent carries which. The brother carries 'the maternally inherited allele', but the paper does not say which of the two variants that is, so his variant row has variant_original_string 'not reported' with inheritance 'inherited maternal'. Parent and brother zygosity left 'not reported' ('carrier'/'carried one of the mutations', no explicit 'heterozygous'). Variant types: missense from 'substitution of cysteine by phenylalanine', nonsense from 'replacement of tyrosine by a termination codon' / 'premature stop' (authors' descriptions, not the HGVS). Checklist T2 hyperintensity marked observed from 'the typical neuroradiological pattern above described' (the Introduction's increased T2 signal of dentate, pallidus, subthalamic nuclei) plus the patient's globus pallidus/dentate abnormalities; the paper does not say 'T2' in the patient's own sentence. Possible internal tension: the Discussion says the patient 'has never experienced movement disorders or psychiatric symptoms' while the Case Report and Results describe hyperactive behavior and attention deficit (and the Discussion lists hyperkineticism and inattention among psychiatric symptoms). I kept attention problems observed (explicit) and used the 'never ... psychiatric symptoms' statement to exclude anxiety, OCD traits, aggression, depression and psychotic symptoms, and the 'never ... movement disorders' statement to exclude dystonia, exertional dyskinesia and hemiballismus; ataxia left not reported ('insufficient coordination' is not called ataxia). 'There was no family history of epilepsy, motor or psychiatric disorders' used as a group statement excluding epilepsy for the brother and both parents. 'while the other investigations were normal' (karyotype, amino acids, creatine) is a group of investigations, not recorded as specific features. Table 1 (GHB levels over treatment time points) and Table 2 (neuropsychological raw scores, garbled column alignment) were not transcribed into features beyond the baseline GHB values; no stacked cells. Age at last evaluation '8.2 years' converted to P8.2Y; the patient was admitted at 4.5 years but no explicit age at diagnosis is stated, so it is not reported. The brother's '16 years old' recorded as age at last evaluation.
